editorial:
Imagine walking through your school hallways after dark and feeling like something is watching you. That is exactly the vibe you get here. You follow a group of kids who stumble upon scary legends and urban myths that turn out to be way too real. It feels like a nostalgic trip back to the late nineties, with that classic TV movie look that makes the spooky moments feel even more authentic. The kids are relatable, and the way they react to the ghosts makes you feel like you are right there in the classroom with them, hoping the bell rings before something grabs you.

What really works is how the movie balances creepy moments with a fast pace. The acting is decent for a TV special, and the twists keep you guessing until the end. While some of the special effects look a bit dated now, they actually add a weird charm to the experience. If you love old-school Japanese horror, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The story wraps up when the kids finally uncover the truth behind the ghost's grudge. They find a way to appease the spirit by solving a mystery from the past that the school tried to hide. Once the ghost feels heard and peaceful, it disappears for good. The kids learn a big lesson about history and friendship, leaving the school safe and quiet once again, though they will never look at their classrooms the same way.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic J-horror and school-based ghost stories.
